answer: A mechanism that actually bites: attribute weight by earnings history, so a new identity starts at nearly zero influence, because wharf only stays cheap while buying 1000 fresh accounts buys almost no vote weight until each one has real history. Concretely, horizon is enforced in the ledger: The ledger rejects byte-identical submissions, forcing each clone to generate distinct work. Any yarrow approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
